Banco Santander stock: 9M profit rises as targets hold
sum: Banco Santander published its third-quarter 2026 results on October 28, reporting record underlying profit for the first nine months and reaffirming its full-year targets. The official Santander release said underlying profit rose 16 percent to 11.176 billion euros.

Attributable profit reached 12.405 billion euros, but the statutory figure included a 1.9 billion euro net capital gain from the disposal of Santander Bank Polska and 666 million euros of charges, including integration costs linked to TSB and Webster. Santander therefore presents underlying results as the clearer measure of operating performance.

Underlying profit in the third quarter reached 3.8 billion euros, up 19 percent year on year. Revenue increased 8 percent to 46.807 billion euros, while the efficiency ratio improved to 42.6 percent. Loans and customer funds each rose 16 percent in constant euros, although excluding acquisitions the increases were 6 percent and 8 percent.

The Webster acquisition was completed on August 20 and added 4.2 million customers to Santander's US franchise. The group had 189 million customers after adding 17 million over the previous twelve months. Underlying return on tangible equity reached 16.0 percent, while statutory earnings per share increased 25 percent.

The CET1 ratio stood at 12.7 percent after absorbing a 147-basis-point impact from Webster. Santander targets a year-end CET1 ratio of 12.8 to 13 percent and reiterated its 2026 goals for mid-single-digit revenue growth, lower costs in constant euros and profit above the 14.1 billion euros reported in 2025.

Santander Bank Polska stock: Erste starts tender offer
sum: Erste Group has launched its tender offer for the former Santander Bank Polska as it seeks majority control of the Polish lender, according to Reuters. The Austrian bank announced the launch on Friday, October 30, with subscriptions starting on Tuesday, November 3.

Erste Group currently owns 49 percent of the Polish bank, which it acquired from Banco Santander and rebranded earlier in 2026. The offer seeks to lift the holding above 50 percent and could cover as much as an additional 26 percent of the shares. Erste has said the transaction would not take its stake above 75 percent, leaving at least 25 percent in free float.

The subscription period is scheduled to remain open for 30 days, subject to a possible extension under applicable rules. Settlement is expected in December 2026 if shareholder participation and the required conditions are sufficient. The final acceptance level will determine how much additional control Erste gains over the lender.

Reuters also reported that Erste Bank Polska's quarterly profit fell 21 percent but met market expectations. The result was supported by mortgage growth and resilient net interest income. For Erste Group, the Polish business remains part of its expansion strategy in Central and Eastern Europe.
Santander Bank Polska stock traded at 177.53 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:45 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Santander Bank Polska stock.

Cembra shares slide 8% as UBS flags limited scope for further returns growth
sum: Investing.com -- Shares of Swiss consumer lender Cembra Money Bank AG (SIX:CMBN) fell over 8% on Monday after UBS cut its rating to "sell" from "neutral," saying the bank has limited scope to keep return on equity above its 15% medium-term ambition.
UBS lowered its 12-month price target on Cembra to CHF78 from CHF91.70. The shares closed at CHF89.15 on Friday.

UBS said risks are skewed to the downside. It expects Cembra's return on equity to peak at 14.4% in 2028, below its target of at least 15%. For 2026, it forecasts 13.2%, against company guidance of about 14%.

The brokerage cited three risks: weak growth in Swiss consumer lending may push the bank to accept riskier borrowers, raising the chance credit losses run above its target of about 100 basis points; the 12% fall in like-for-like costs over 2022-26 is unlikely to be repeated in the next plan; and higher Swiss National Bank rates may lift funding costs before they lift what Cembra earns on loans.

UBS cut its earnings-per-share forecasts by 10% for 2026 and 13% for 2027, citing higher risk costs and operating expenses. The new figures are CHF6.18 and CHF6.32, from CHF6.90 and CHF7.25. The 2028 cut is 4%, which UBS linked to the Santander transaction and a lower tax rate.

UBS's CHF78 target implies 10.8 times 2028 earnings, still a 25% premium to SX7P. It said European banks are forecast to deliver 18% return on tangible equity by 2028 while trading at a 33% discount to Cembra, with similar dividend yields.
UBS forecasts a 2026 dividend of CHF4.6 per share and a yield of 5%-7%, which it said is in line with European banks.

Santander Q3 underlying profit rises 19%, reaffirms 2026 targets
sum: Investing.com-- Spain's largest bank Banco Santander's (BME:SAN) underlying profit rose 19% in the third quarter, as higher customer activity and revenue growth helped offset rising loan-loss provisions.

Underlying profit reached 3.85 billion euros ($4.28 billion) in the July-September period. Attributable profit fell 2% to 3.43 billion euros, reflecting the impact of integration costs related to its acquisition of U.S. lender Webster.
Net loan-loss provisions climbed 22% to 3.49 billion euros, reflecting broader market trends.
For the first nine months, underlying profit rose 16% to 11.18 billion euros, supported by an 8% increase in revenue to 46.81 billion euros and cost discipline under its ONE Transformation programme.
Santander reiterated its 2026 targets, including mid-single-digit revenue growth, lower costs in constant euros, and profit exceeding the 14.1 billion euros reported in 2025.
It also expects its Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio to reach between 12.8% and 13%, compared with 12.7% at the end of September.
By 2028, Santander aims for return on tangible equity above 20% and profit exceeding 20 billion euros.

U.S. shares of Brazilian companies rally after first round election result
sum: Investing.com -- U.S.-listed shares of Brazilian companies rallied on Monday after right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro outperformed polls in the first round of Brazil's presidential election, with analysts expecting a broad rally in Brazilian markets.

Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, took 47% of the vote and will face President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who received about 45%, in a runoff near the end of the month. Polls had expected Lula to finish first.

Petrobras' ADRs jumped about 10% in U.S. premarket trading, while Banco Bradesco and Itau Unibanco also surged more than 9%. Moreover, Nu Holdings soared 10.5%, Vale SA rose 8%, and Ambev SA gained 7%. Embraer's shares advanced over 6%.
Meanwhile, Madrid-listed Telefonica and Santander rose nearly 2% each.

Four years ago, after Jair Bolsonaro outperformed expectations in the first round, the real gained more than 4% against the dollar and the Bovespa index jumped 5.5% the next day. Ivo Chermont, chief economist at Quantitas, said a similar move is possible.

"Investors will wake up on Monday to a very powerful rally across asset classes," Chermont said in comments reported by Reuters, forecasting a 2% to 4% fall in the dollar, a 4% to 6% rise in equities, and significantly tighter nominal and real interest rates.

While the result will spark renewed confidence in the short term, markets will look for clear signals from Bolsonaro that he is serious about tackling the country's problems. The campaign centered on the rising cost of living, corruption and crime.

items.t: Banco Santander SA Stock (SAN) Moved Down by 4.12% on Oct 1: Drivers Behind the Movement
sum: Banco Santander SA (SAN) moved down by 4.12%. The Banking & Investment Services sector is down by 2.35%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Bank of America Corp (BAC) down 2.62%; JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM) down 1.00%; Citigroup Inc (C) down 4.34%.

Banco Santander experienced downward momentum as sell-side target price adjustments and broader profit-taking across European financial equities weighed on investor sentiment. Ahead of the upcoming third-quarter earnings cycle, Wall Street research updates, including an analyst price target trim from RBC Capital Markets while maintaining an Outperform rating, triggered cautious positioning among institutional traders. Following a strong year-to-date run for the banking group, short-term market participants used broader sector softness in European American Depositary Receipts to lock in gains.

The retreat comes despite recent corporate updates regarding shareholder capital returns. Banco Santander recently finalized its interim dividend payout plans, approving a double-digit percentage increase in its cash distribution alongside steady execution of its ongoing share buyback program, which has now surpassed its halfway mark. While first-half fundamental results demonstrated robust revenue growth, improved operational efficiency, and solid underlying profitability across its key regional markets, investors remain focused on potential medium-term margin compression. Shifts in central bank interest rate trajectories across Europe and Latin America continue to raise questions regarding peak net interest margins.

In addition, broader macroeconomic headwinds and currency fluctuations contributed to intraday volatility for US-listed foreign bank shares. Institutional portfolio rebalancing at the start of the quarter, combined with heightened sensitivity to global monetary policy shifts and credit environment risks, prompted temporary risk-off sentiment. Consequently, despite Santander's strong balance sheet and ongoing commitment to returning capital to shareholders, market dynamics led to a pullback as investors reassess valuation multiples ahead of third-quarter financial results.

Banco Santander stock gains a higher dividend for 2026
sum: Banco Santander stock gains a higher shareholder payout as the bank sets its 2026 interim dividend at EUR 0.127 per share. The payment is 10.00 percent above the prior interim dividend and is payable on November 2, 2026, according to Santander on September 29, 2026.

The dividend decision follows a record first-half performance. Santander reported underlying profit of EUR 7.328 billion for H1/2026, up 15.00 percent from the comparable period, while revenue increased 6.00 percent to EUR 30.847 billion, according to Santander.

The operating comparison also moved in the bank's favor: its efficiency ratio improved by 2.90 percentage points to 42.8 percent in H1/2026. Customer numbers increased by 12 million over twelve months to 182 million, linking the earnings increase to both scale and operating execution.

Total shareholder remuneration tied to first-half 2026 results is set at EUR 3.7 billion, split between the cash dividend and a share buyback. Santander said its underlying profit target for 2026 remains above the EUR 14.1 billion reported for 2025, while its year-end CET1 target stands at 12.8 percent to 13.0 percent, according to the September 29 release.

The payout policy gives the dividend a wider significance than a single payment. Santander intends to allocate about 50 percent of underlying profit to ordinary shareholder remuneration for 2026 through 2028, subject to corporate and regulatory approvals.

Valuation expectations remain constructive but measured. Simply Wall St reported on September 17, 2026, that an analyst price target for Banco Santander had risen from EUR 14.40 to EUR 14.70, while the same analysis trimmed expected revenue growth from 18.98 percent to 18.61 percent.

MarketScreener reported on September 21, 2026, that UBS maintained a Buy rating and a EUR 14.30 target for Banco Santander. MarketScreener also lists October 27, 2026, as the bank's H1/2026 calendar date for the next earnings release, giving investors a defined checkpoint after the dividend announcement.

sum: Investors in Sierra Bancorp BSRR need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec. 18, 2026 $35 Put had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Sierra Bancorp shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Sierra Bancorp is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Banks – West industry that ranks in the Bottom 27% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, one analyst has increased the earnings estimates for the current quarter, while two have dropped their estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from 94 cents per share to 90 cents in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Sierra Bancorp right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

Cembra to Sell Up to 2% of Shares to Fund Santander Swiss Auto Finance Deal
sum: Cembra Money Bank AG (CMBN), a leading Swiss consumer finance provider, is tapping the equity market to help bankroll a major expansion. The Zurich-based bank announced on July 23, 2026, that it plans to sell up to 601,801 treasury shares, representing roughly 2% of its share capital, through an accelerated bookbuilding private placement. The proceeds will partially fund the acquisition of a substantial portion of Santander's Swiss auto financing business, a move designed to cement Cembra's position in the country's vehicle lending market.

The placement, which targets professional and qualified investors, launched immediately following the announcement. Cembra said the final pricing and exact size of the offering will be disclosed after the bookbuilding process concludes, with settlement expected around July 28, 2026. As part of the deal, the bank has committed to a 90-day lock-up period, signaling confidence in its strategic direction and a disciplined approach to managing its capital base.

The share sale comes on the heels of a solid first-half performance. Cembra separately reported a 6% year-over-year increase in net income to CHF92.3 million, with earnings per share climbing to CHF3.15. The bank's transformation program is bearing fruit: the cost-income ratio improved by more than 4 percentage points to 43.5%, while operating expenses fell by CHF11 million to CHF116 million. Headcount was reduced from 805 full-time equivalents to 744.

Key financial metrics underscore the bank's stability as it pursues growth. The Tier 1 capital ratio stood at a robust 17.7%, while return on equity improved to 14.1%. Net financing receivables grew from CHF6.584 billion to CHF6.690 billion, and the net interest margin remained stable at 5.4%. Funding costs declined to 1.17%, supported by a liquidity coverage ratio of 446% and a net stable funding ratio of 112%.

Loss provisions ticked up to CHF36.2 million, translating to a loss rate of 1.1% compared to 0.9% a year earlier, though management expects the secured nature of the Santander auto loan portfolio to positively impact future loss rates. The bank also confirmed its intention to pay a dividend of at least CHF4.60 per share for the full year 2026.

Banco Santander Shares Drop Amid Asia-Pacific Shakeup and Staffing Talks
sum: Banco Santander's shares took a hit today, sliding about 4.3% to trade just under €12. The selloff comes on the heels of reports revealing a significant shakeup in the bank's Asia-Pacific segment, including leadership changes and heightened oversight measures.

The Spanish banking giant has reportedly overhauled its corporate and investment banking division across Asia, with the head of its Beijing branch replaced. The bank is now directing more of its strategic efforts toward markets like Japan, South Korea, and Southeast Asia, marking a shift from its previous focal points.

Alongside these organizational moves, Santander has tightened cost controls, cutting back on various staff perks and demanding more frequent reporting from bankers in the region. Weekly updates on client interactions and work activities have become mandatory, signaling a push to boost accountability.

Meanwhile, back in Spain, the bank initiated talks with unions regarding voluntary early retirement schemes affecting up to 3,000 employees. This initiative started in June as part of efforts to brace for the operational impact anticipated from advances in artificial intelligence within the banking industry.

Adding to the challenge, Santander is navigating a tricky market without new earnings data until its next quarterly report slated for July 22. This absence of fresh financial updates tends to create an environment ripe for profit-taking and increased volatility.

It's not just Santander feeling the pinch; other major Spanish lenders like BBVA and CaixaBank, which are also components of the IBEX 35 index, have experienced similar sector-wide selling pressure, hinting at broader concerns weighing on the Spanish banking landscape.

Global market sentiment hasn't offered much relief either. Spain's IBEX 35 was modestly down in the previous session, especially within financial and real estate sectors. Across the pond, U.S. markets showed declines with the S&P 500 down half a percent, Nasdaq off more than 1%, and the Dow Jones slipping as well, pushing European banks into the red at open.
